doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Future plans, travel schedule and practicing on his new Steinway
summary: A follow-up trio record, upcoming festivals, and casual practice on a new Steinway.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You’ll have to go and see what you did on that. See if the audience was with you that night too. Well this has really been fascinating talking to you, and I’m so glad that we got to hear you last night. You just said that you’re not in great need of putting out a new record, but I hope you do soon.
Well I probably will because the response to this one has been great, and I’m pretty sure that I’ll be doing something as a follow-up to this.
Most likely another trio setting, yes.
Where are you off to — I’m sorry to interrupt you.
A Tribute to My Piano Friends Volume II.
Are you off to any distance soon, traveling?

No, I’m in the middle of a sort of like a late winter-early spring vacation you know, just being around home. The thing last night for Marian was the first thing I’ve done in maybe three weeks, so I’m just kind of taking it easy. I had a very, very busy winter. I spent almost a month in Germany and two weeks in Paris and I was in Japan in December, and I’ve really been moving around, and so sometimes you just have to sit still and just enjoy, and that’s what I’m doing right now. I think my next thing out of the country would probably be I have some festivals to do this summer in Europe and in Canada, the Ottawa Festival I’m going to do and I think the Toronto Festival and there’s a possibility of festivals in Wales, JVC Festivals in France again, and I’m supposed to go to Italy sometime this year, and a club date in Switzerland and things like this, but nothing in the near future, in the next couple of weeks.
When you have three weeks off, are you a practicer?
Not too much, but I’m a little more than I used to be because I just bought a new piano just before Christmas.
I was going to ask what’s your preference in pianos?

I bought a Steinway. Steinway is, that is my preference. So I’m playing this one pretty good, but I’m not a diligent practicer like three or four hours a day, no. I just sit down and play something, I get up and go and come back to it later. I keep it open so all I’ve got to do is sit down and play.
